gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-osage: Nippo stands tall with small letters nearly as big as its capitals, each stroke looking cut from wire. And Noto Sans Osage fills the line with inflated lowercase bowls and sweeping curves that stay open.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-osmanya: Wire-cut strokes of one single width give Nippo a technical, sharp-edged look up top, while Noto Sans Osmanya turns easy, wide s shapes below. Lowercase that outsizes its capitals is the pair's strongest hook.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-pahawh-hmong: Noto Sans Pahawh Hmong reads tall and open, with a high-set x-height and rounds that gap like a cracked bangle. Nippo's ribbon-cut, constant-width strokes make the sharper partner.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-pau-cin-hau: Clean and technical, Nippo draws its stems and arches at identical thickness, with small letters nearly as tall as capitals. And Noto Sans Pau Cin Hau echoes that short step up to the capitals but lets its open-ended curves breathe.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-phagspa: Nippo draws horizontals as thick as its verticals, so the small letters look cut from wire and almost capital-sized. But Noto Sans PhagsPa softens the page with see-through c openings and a gentle bump up to its capitals.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-phoenician: Nippo keeps one stroke thickness everywhere, and its small letters stand nearly as tall as its capitals, like wire bent into shape. Noto Sans Phoenician follows with wide-ended s curves and generous lowercase height.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-psalter-pahlav: Nippo is all wire-cut strokes and proud small letters. Its stems and arches share one thickness, while Noto Sans Psalter Pahlavi does the friendlier work with gaping e mouths and barely rising capitals.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-rejang: Noto Sans Rejang opens its lowercase counters like wide glass portholes, with clear gaps in c, e, s, and a. Yet Nippo gives the pair its edge, with the single-width trail of a rolling-ball pen and nearly capital-sized small letters.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-runic: Sign-shop vinyl cut to a single line width is the look of Nippo, with small letters almost as tall as its capitals. Noto Sans Runic answers with a big x-height and curves that never close back on themselves.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-samaritan: Wire-sharp and compact, Nippo draws bowls and stems at the same weight, with small letters almost capital height. Yet Noto Sans Samaritan, hefty in the lowercase and full of daylight inside its curves, would carry paragraphs with an approachable ease.
